name: cloud-infra-mcp
description: C3 MCP Server — Cloud Control Center MCP transport (stdio + HTTP)

legacy_aliases._dns_aliases_deferred: superapp-mcp.mesh and cloud-superapp-mcp.mesh stay with the old cloud-superapp-mcp container until the merged peers-control tools are verified (needs SUPERAPP_FLEET_TOKEN in this service secrets); claiming them earlier rendered two Caddy sites for one host (ambiguous site definition).
legacy_aliases._doc: #1495 cloudy-android-mcp (cloud-superapp-mcp) is merged into this server as the peers-control tool group. Its old names stay as aliases for one release (#1450 alias policy): the old DNS names and the base paths /cloud-superapp-mcp and /cloudy-android-mcp are rewritten by the edge to this container's /mcp-android endpoint, which serves the same server plus the old `superapp` + `superapp_help` dispatchers so a client keeps its tool names. Remove with the other #1450 aliases and delete infra-api_cloud-superapp-mcp.

native_build._cmd_comment: cloudflared FIRST: upstream static release 2026.9.2, sha256 pinned per arch (arm64 is what ships; amd64 only so an x86 builder fails closed instead of fetching an unverified binary). wrangler is NOT fetched here: it is an exact-pinned dependency in code/package.json, so npm ci installs it with the lockfile's sha512 integrity (workerd/esbuild arm64 optional deps included); the trailing --version proves it runs on the target arch. Both back the Cloudflare bridge tools in mcp/tools/cloudflare.ts.
native_build.cmd: A=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && case $A in arm64) S=39f23e7c55ce2c2e502a0b3e070b978bf69135b19246b5b7581dadb94cf2144d;; amd64) S=ea2c9bb2d5017a796b64bf36e605d727accf76a5500014bb12952ce11ae1f932;; *) echo "cloudflared: unsupported arch $A"; exit 1;; esac && curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/cloudflared https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/download/2026.9.2/cloudflared-linux-$A && echo "$S  /usr/local/bin/cloudflared" | sha256sum -c - && chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/cloudflared && cloudflared --version && pip install --break-system-packages --no-cache-dir oci-cli awscli && npm ci --omit=dev && npm install tsx && ./node_modules/.bin/wrangler --version
native_build.apt: ca-certificates openssh-client iputils-ping curl git python3 python3-pip build-essential dnsutils openssl netcat-openbsd

env_config._browser_doc: #1540 browser.* cloudflare backend (Cloudflare Browser Run REST): max Cloudflare calls per UTC day, max estimated spend per day (USD, browser hours at the paid rate) and how long a domain that needed Cloudflare is remembered. Secrets by NAME in .secrets: CF_BROWSER_ACCOUNT_ID (or CF_ACCOUNT_ID), CF_BROWSER_API_TOKEN (or CF_API_TOKEN) with the Browser Run - Edit permission, OPENROUTER_API_KEY for browser.json on container/phone.

runtime._why_init: cloud-infra-mcp spawns ssh/git/curl/dig children concurrently via execAsync. Without docker-init (tini) as PID 1, zombie reaping doesn't happen and pids_limit is exhausted within days -> 'sh: 0: Cannot fork' on healthcheck.
runtime._why_pids_limit: ssh-exec + git-clone + curl all fan out concurrently across ~24 VM/service targets. Default 256 is too tight; 1024 leaves safe headroom with tini reaping orphans.

mcp.description: Cloud health, DevOps operations, workflows, cost tracking, security scanning, observability, front-end deployment, plus the peers-control phone tools (merged from cloudy-android-mcp). Tools are served as the legacy infra_* dispatchers and as the Cloud-C3 app's hierarchy (c3_infra, c3_containers, c3_home, c3_ops, c3_observ, c3_configs, c3_tree).

ssh._phones_doc: #1495 MERGED from cloudy-android-mcp (cloud-superapp-mcp): the peers-control tool group dials the phones from here. THE ONE declaration of the phones this MCP dials (two phones since #573: the S21+ on wg client `termux` 10.0.0.9 and the A37 on wg client `samsung-a37` 10.0.0.10). Each phone's mesh addresses and peer key are NOT restated here: `wg_client` names its row in cloud-infra config.json#native.wireguard.clients (the same row superapp-users.json peers point at), and the derive resolves it into /opt/ssh-keys/cloud-infra-mcp/config. `alias` is the phone's fleet name; for each phone and each door in `doors` the MCP dials <alias><suffix> (v4) and <alias><suffix>-v6. extra_hosts below is exactly that expansion — test/test-superapp-hosts.sh fails on any drift, and on a SUPERAPP_PHONES alias that is not declared here. Every tool takes `phone` (alias or id); omitted, the phone that answered most recently is tried first, then the rest, and every result names the phone that answered.
ssh._extra_hosts_doc: Ssh aliases the MCP dials (expanded from phones x doors; SUPERAPP_PHONES in src/compose.nix picks the order). The phone's sshd is provided by OUR terminals (cloud-u-android ac_cloud-nix-on-droid / ac_cloud-termux; ports and users as declared in ac_cloud-myterminal/data/terminal-targets.json: nix 8024 user nix-on-droid, termux 8023 user termux). Address = each phone's wg0 mesh client (phones[].wg_client) (config.json native.wireguard.clients), resolved by the derive into /opt/ssh-keys/cloud-infra-mcp/config. MESH ONLY: the phone has no public ssh route by design (sshd is reached over WireGuard; ide-endpoints.json: public surface is 443+51820+25), so there is no phone-pub. The key offered is vault_id_rsa (keys above); it is authorised on the phone by cloud-u-linux da__my-konsole/termux/authorized_keys. test/test-superapp-hosts.sh fails if an alias in SUPERAPP_HOSTS has no entry here.
